facts.value: Physical exercises are generally grouped into three types: Aerobic exercise, Anaerobic exercise, and Flexibility exercises.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Aerobic exercise is any physical activity that uses large muscle groups and causes the body to use more oxygen than it would while resting. The goal of aerobic exercise is to increase cardiovascular endurance.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Examples of aerobic exercise include running, cycling, swimming, brisk walking, skipping rope, rowing, hiking, dancing, playing tennis, continuous training, and long distance running.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Anaerobic exercise includes strength and resistance training, which can firm, strengthen, and increase muscle mass, as well as improve bone density, balance, and coordination.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Examples of strength exercises include push-ups, pull-ups, lunges, squats, and bench press. Anaerobic exercise also includes weight training, functional training, eccentric training, interval training, sprinting, and high-intensity interval training.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Flexibility exercises stretch and lengthen muscles. Activities such as stretching help to improve joint flexibility and keep muscles limber.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: The goal is to improve the range of motion which can reduce the chance of injury.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Physical exercise can also include training that focuses on accuracy, agility, power, and speed.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Types of exercise can also be classified as dynamic or static. Dynamic exercises, such as steady running, tend to lower diastolic blood pressure during exercise, while static exercises, such as weight-lifting, can cause systolic pressure to rise significantly during the performance of the exercise.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc
